name: Ledger total
rule: SUM(quantity x price) over every row in the file.
pitfall: Mixes product sales with postage, bank charges, manual entries, bad-debt adjustments and test items.

name: Gross sales
rule: Product lines on non-cancelled invoices, positive quantity and price. Duplicates kept.
pitfall: Ignores returns, so it only ever looks better than the cash that stays.

name: Net sales
rule: All product lines including cancellation credits, dated when the credit was issued. Duplicates kept.
pitfall: Duplicate lines (including the sheet overlap) still inflate it; returns hit the month they are credited, not the month of the sale.

name: Net clean revenue
rule: R3 after removing exact duplicate lines (same invoice, item, quantity, price, timestamp, customer).
pitfall: A true repeat scan on one invoice is indistinguishable from a duplicate, so this can undercount slightly.

name: Identified-customer revenue
rule: R4 restricted to rows with a Customer ID.
pitfall: Silently drops guest checkouts, so it shrinks whenever guest share grows.

name: Any record
rule: Distinct Customer IDs on any row in the month, including returns and fees.
pitfall: A customer who only returned something, or only paid a fee, counts as active.

name: Purchasing customers
rule: Distinct Customer IDs with at least one purchase line (product, non-cancelled, positive quantity and price) in the month.
pitfall: Guest checkouts have no ID and are not counted here; the dictionary reports them next to it.

name: Net-positive customers
rule: Distinct Customer IDs whose net clean spend in the month is above zero.
pitfall: A customer who buys and returns the same value in a month disappears.

name: Buyers incl. guests
rule: A2 plus one buyer for every distinct guest invoice.
pitfall: A guest who orders three times is three buyers, so the count drifts up as guest checkout grows.

name: Trailing 90-day active
rule: Distinct Customer IDs with a purchase in the 90 days up to month end. Needs 90 days of history, so the first months are blank.
pitfall: Smooth by construction: it reacts to a change about three months late.

name: Ledger per invoice
rule: R1 divided by every distinct invoice number, including cancellations and fee-only invoices.
pitfall: Cancellation invoices lower the numerator and add to the denominator at the same time.

name: Clean gross per invoice
rule: Gross product value of purchase invoices (duplicates removed) divided by the count of those invoices.
pitfall: One invoice is one order, so a customer who splits a basket looks like two smaller orders.

name: Net per invoice
rule: R4 (net of returns) divided by the count of purchase invoices.
pitfall: Numerator subtracts returns, denominator ignores the matching invoices, so the ratio is biased down.

name: Median invoice value
rule: Median gross product value of purchase invoices.
pitfall: Hides wholesale orders, which is where most of the money is.

name: Value per consolidated order
rule: Clean gross value divided by orders, where one order is one customer on one day (one invoice for guests).
pitfall: Merges real separate orders placed on the same day.
